articles.title: Antidepressants Under the Microscope: The Benefits They Oversell and the Harms They Bury
articles.summary: As antidepressant prescriptions hit record highs globally, a critical analysis exposes the gap between marketed efficacy and real-world outcomes — including dependency, withdrawal, and blunted emotional response that regulators have long downplayed. The serotonin hypothesis underpinning these drugs was quietly abandoned by researchers while prescribing rates continued to climb. Patients are being medicated based on a theory the field itself no longer believes.

articles.title: Vitamin B3 Shrinks Glioblastoma Immune Suppression — Mainstream Oncology Still Pushing Chemo Alone
articles.summary: A small but striking trial finds high-dose niacin kept 82% of glioblastoma patients progression-free at six months by reactivating immune cells the tumor had suppressed — a metabolic intervention that costs pennies compared to standard-of-care biologics. Researchers believe the mechanism involves restoring exhausted tumor-infiltrating lymphocytes, a finding that cuts against the pharmaceutical industry's billion-dollar immunotherapy franchise. Expect this data to stay buried in conference abstracts while patent-protected alternatives dominate oncology guidelines.

articles.title: Progesterone as a Depression Treatment: The Hormone Therapy Big Pharma Won't Fund
articles.summary: Emerging research links chronic stress-driven cortisol dysregulation to depression and points to progesterone as a neuroactive steroid capable of restoring balance — without the dependency and blunted affect of SSRIs. This approach remains clinically marginalized despite a plausible biological mechanism, largely because progesterone is off-patent and cannot be monopolized. The psychiatric establishment's refusal to fund comparative trials against SSRIs is not an oversight — it is a business decision.

articles.title: Medicare Fraud in Plain Sight: Independence Blue Cross Pays $22.5M for Faking Diagnoses to Pocket Federal Dollars
articles.summary: Independence Blue Cross has agreed to pay $22.5 million to settle federal allegations that it retained Medicare Advantage overpayments generated by unsupported diagnosis codes — a textbook upcoding scheme that inflated risk scores to extract more taxpayer money. This is not a paperwork error; it is systematic fraud against a program serving the elderly and disabled, enabled by the opaque Medicare Advantage audit system that watchdogs have repeatedly flagged as broken. No executives are named, no criminal referrals announced — just a check and a press release.

articles.title: FDA Consistency Problem: Two Rejections, One Resubmission, Zero Accountability on Lymphoma Cell Therapy
articles.summary: Tab-cel, a cell therapy for rare post-transplant lymphoma, has been resubmitted to the FDA using the same single-arm study design the agency previously criticized — raising sharp questions about whether FDA evidentiary standards are principled or negotiated. Two prior rejections did not stop the manufacturer from returning with essentially the same data package, and the FDA appears poised to accept it on the third attempt. This is regulatory capture dressed up as science: the standard moves to meet the product, not the other way around.

articles.title: ICE Quietly Deletes Medical Neglect Reports Documenting Detainee Deaths — Government Erasing Its Own Evidence
articles.summary: Internal reports flagging medical care that 'deviated beyond safe limits' in dozens of ICE detainee deaths have been scrubbed from government servers, eliminating documentation of systemic failures that should trigger federal investigations. The deletion of adverse event records by a government agency is precisely the kind of data suppression that, in a clinical context, would constitute research misconduct and obstruction. When the government erases its own death records, the cover-up is the story.

articles.title: Beta Bionics Securities Fraud: Investors Blindsided by Hidden Medical Device Safety Failures
articles.summary: A securities fraud class action has been filed against Beta Bionics after its stock collapsed 37% on disclosure that the company allegedly misrepresented the safety and efficacy of its iLet insulin-delivery device to investors — and by extension to the patients depending on it. If the allegations hold, this is not just investor fraud: patients were using a device whose real safety profile was concealed from the market that was supposed to price that risk. The FDA's post-market surveillance system, once again, failed to catch it first.

articles.title: Dental Pulp Stem Cells Reverse Stroke Damage in Mice — Will This Research Ever Reach a Clinical Trial?
articles.summary: Korean researchers at Chonnam National University have demonstrated that the secretome of human dental pulp stem cells significantly attenuates oxidative stress and neuroinflammation in post-stroke mouse models, accelerating functional recovery through mechanisms distinct from any approved pharmaceutical. Stem cell secretome research occupies a therapeutic no-man's-land: too promising to ignore, too unpatentable to attract serious industry funding, and too far outside the approved neurology narrative to reach mainstream clinical pipelines. This data will sit in a journal while stroke survivors are handed blood thinners and told to manage expectations.

articles.title: Lancet Goes Full Propaganda: Medical Journal of Record Abandons Science for Narrative Control
articles.summary: Investigative journalist Maryanne Demasi at Brownstone Institute documents how The Lancet — once a cornerstone of medical publishing — has descended into ideologically driven editorial decisions that betray its scientific mission. The piece names the journal's pattern of publishing politically convenient conclusions while sidelining inconvenient data. This is institutional capture of the highest-impact medical literature in the world.

articles.title: SIDS-Vaccine Paper Retracted After Five Years — Censorship Disguised as Peer Review
articles.summary: A peer-reviewed paper analyzing VAERS data for a potential link between vaccines and Sudden Infant Death Syndrome was allowed to stand for five years before being quietly retracted — not for data fraud, but for reaching the wrong conclusions. Jessica Rose at Brownstone Institute exposes the retraction as a political act, not a scientific one. When VAERS-based safety signals become unpublishable, the entire pharmacovigilance system becomes theater.

articles.title: COVID Origin Bombshell: New Evidence Points to Engineered Virus and Coordinated Vaccine Development Timeline
articles.summary: A new Brownstone Institute analysis by Jim Haslam presents fresh documentary evidence clarifying the parallel timelines of SARS-CoV-2 development and the mRNA vaccine program, raising direct questions about gain-of-function research and pre-planned countermeasures. The piece draws on recently surfaced records to argue that the official origin narrative was never scientifically defensible. The implications for Fauci, NIH, and EcoHealth Alliance are profound.

articles.title: Vitamin B3 Obliterates Glioblastoma Progression in 82% of Trial Patients — So Why Isn't This Headline News?
articles.summary: A small but striking clinical trial shows high-dose niacin keeping 82% of glioblastoma patients progression-free at six months — a cancer with a median survival under 15 months on standard of care alone. Researchers believe niacin reactivates immune cells that tumors systematically suppress, pointing to a metabolic and immunological mechanism that has been chronically underfunded. A cheap, unpatentable vitamin outperforming billion-dollar oncology drugs is precisely the kind of result the industry has no incentive to amplify.

articles.title: Progesterone Suppressed as Depression Treatment While SSRIs Reign — Follow the Patent Money
articles.summary: Research covered by Mercola.com details how chronic stress-driven depression has a measurable hormonal component — specifically progesterone deficiency — that could offer a safer, non-addictive treatment pathway. This data has existed for years but receives a fraction of the funding and publication support given to SSRI trials backed by Pfizer, Eli Lilly, and AstraZeneca. Bioidentical hormones can't be patented, so they don't get studied — and patients stay on drugs that carry black-box suicide warnings.

articles.title: Mitochondrial Dysfunction at the Root of Cancer and Chronic Disease — The Research Big Pharma Doesn't Want Mainstream
articles.summary: Mercola.com synthesizes a growing body of peer-reviewed research linking mitochondrial failure and chronic inflammation as upstream drivers of cancer — a metabolic theory of disease that directly challenges the somatic mutation model that justifies trillion-dollar chemotherapy markets. If cancer is primarily a metabolic disease, dietary and mitochondrial interventions become first-line tools, not adjuncts. The oncology-industrial complex has actively marginalized this research for decades.

articles.title: Insurance Giant to Pay $22.5M for Medicare Advantage Fraud — The Upcoding Scam That Bleeds Taxpayers Dry
articles.summary: Independence Blue Cross will pay $22.5 million to settle allegations that it retained Medicare Advantage overpayments tied to diagnosis codes that lacked clinical support — a form of systematic billing fraud that inflates insurer profits at taxpayer expense. This case is one data point in a well-documented pattern of Medicare Advantage upcoding that federal auditors have flagged repeatedly while enforcement has remained tepid. The patients whose records were manipulated to inflate risk scores never consented to being turned into profit centers.

articles.title: FDA Inconsistency Laid Bare: Two Rejections, One Resubmission, and Shifting Goalposts on Evidence Standards
articles.summary: After rejecting tabelecleucel twice, the FDA is now reconsidering the rare lymphoma cell therapy based on a single-arm study design it previously questioned — raising serious questions about whether FDA approval standards are scientifically principled or negotiable depending on manufacturer persistence and commercial pressure. Medical Daily's analysis highlights how the agency's evidentiary bar moves in ways that cannot be explained by science alone. When approval standards flex, patient safety becomes a variable, not a guarantee.

articles.title: Nature Medicine Finally Admits Replication Crisis Is Systemic — Science's Credibility Is Burning
articles.summary: A new review in Nature Medicine acknowledges that reproducibility failures are endemic across biomedical research, with inconsistent implementation of reproducible practices persisting despite years of warnings. This is the same peer-review apparatus that rubber-stamped COVID policy science, fast-tracked mRNA trials, and buried dissenting studies. When the establishment's own flagship journal admits the foundation is cracked, every mandated intervention built on that foundation deserves re-examination.

articles.title: Vitamin B3 Kills Glioblastoma Cells the Chemo Industry Won't Touch — 82% Progression-Free at Six Months
articles.summary: High-dose niacin showed an 82% progression-free survival rate at six months in a small glioblastoma trial by reactivating immune cells the tumor had suppressed — a metabolic mechanism that oncology orthodoxy has ignored for decades in favor of high-margin chemotherapy. Glioblastoma kills nearly everyone it touches within 15 months under standard of care, yet cheap, off-patent vitamin interventions targeting immune exhaustion receive no serious funding. Follow the patent trail.

articles.title: SSRIs Alter Cancer Immunotherapy Outcomes — Psychiatry and Oncology Collide in Data Big Pharma Doesn't Want Integrated
articles.summary: A PLOS Medicine target trial emulation finds that SSRI use among cancer patients receiving immune checkpoint inhibitors produces measurably different outcomes compared to benzodiazepine users — raising urgent questions about how pervasive psychiatric medication is silently confounding oncology trial results. The pharmaceutical industry profits from both drug classes and has every financial incentive to keep these silos sealed. This is the kind of cross-drug interaction signal that never makes it into the package insert.

articles.title: Estrogen Dominance, Histamine, and Endotoxin: The Hormonal Framework Medicine Refuses to Teach
articles.summary: Researcher Georgi Dinkov outlines the biochemical cascade linking estrogen dominance to histamine overload, serotonin dysregulation, and gut-derived endotoxin — a framework that explains chronic fatigue, infertility, and inflammatory disease without a single patented drug. Mainstream endocrinology dismisses estrogen dominance as fringe despite a mountain of mechanistic evidence, because correctly diagnosing it would eliminate the market for antidepressants, antihistamines, and hormonal contraceptives prescribed to manage its downstream symptoms. This is suppression by willful ignorance.

articles.title: Progesterone Reverses Stress-Induced Depression — But Psychiatry Would Rather Sell You an SSRI for Life
articles.summary: Research highlighted by Mercola identifies progesterone as a direct neurological intervention for chronic stress-induced depression, working on the very brain pathways that chronic stress degrades. This mechanism is well-documented in the literature but systematically ignored by psychiatric guidelines, which funnel patients toward SSRIs with black-box warnings and documented withdrawal syndromes rather than toward bioidentical hormonal correction. The patent status of progesterone versus SSRIs explains everything you need to know about which one gets the research dollars.

articles.title: Independence Blue Cross Caught Keeping $22.5M in Medicare Advantage Fraud — The Diagnosis Code Scam Exposed
articles.summary: Independence Blue Cross will pay $22.5 million to settle federal allegations that it retained overpayments generated by unsupported diagnosis codes in its Medicare Advantage program — a systemic fraud that inflates federal payments by making patient populations appear sicker than they are. This is not an isolated incident; Medicare Advantage upcoding is a known, documented industry-wide practice that transfers billions from taxpayers to insurers annually. CMS has the data and has chosen, year after year, not to act at scale.

articles.title: ICE Deletes Its Own Medical Neglect Death Reports — Government Destroying Evidence of Lethal Care Failures
articles.summary: The Department of Homeland Security's ICE division quietly deleted internal review reports documenting medical care that 'deviated beyond safe limits' in dozens of in-custody deaths — a deliberate destruction of accountability records covering government-caused patient harm. These were not leaked documents or whistleblower memos; they were ICE's own findings, scrubbed from public access after they became inconvenient. When a federal agency deletes its own death investigations, that is not bureaucratic housekeeping — it is evidence suppression.

articles.title: Beta Bionics Allegedly Lied to Investors About iLet Device Safety and FDA Compliance — Patients Were the Guinea Pigs
articles.summary: Two separate securities fraud class actions allege that Beta Bionics misled investors about the safety, efficacy, and regulatory standing of its iLet automated insulin delivery device, with the stock cratering over 37% when the truth emerged. When a medical device company allegedly deceives its own investors about FDA compliance, the patients using that device in their bodies deserve to know they were operating on a foundation of potential fraud. The FDA's device approval pathway has long been criticized for being captured by the very industry it regulates.

articles.title: Replication Crisis Confirmed in Print: Nature Medicine Admits Biomedical Research Is Systematically Unreliable
articles.summary: Nature Medicine's own review concedes that reproducibility — the bedrock of trustworthy science — is routinely failing across biomedical research, with no consistent standards enforced. This is the same research infrastructure that produced rushed COVID therapeutics, approved psychiatric drugs on shaky trials, and set dietary guidelines that shaped a generation. The system isn't broken — it was never fixed.

articles.title: Vitamin B3 Shows 82% Progression-Free Rate in Glioblastoma Trial — Will the Oncology Cartel Bury It?
articles.summary: A small but striking trial shows high-dose niacin (vitamin B3) keeping 82% of glioblastoma patients progression-free at six months by reviving immune cells suppressed by the tumor microenvironment. Glioblastoma has a median survival of 15 months under standard care — a number that hasn't meaningfully moved in decades despite billions in drug spending. A cheap, unpatentable vitamin showing this signal deserves urgent investigation, not footnote status.

articles.title: SSRIs Interfere With Cancer Immunotherapy — A Drug Interaction the Prescribing Industry Didn't Want You to Know
articles.summary: New research published in PLOS Medicine reveals that SSRI use in cancer patients receiving immune checkpoint inhibitors is associated with meaningfully different outcomes compared to benzodiazepine users — raising serious questions about drug-drug interactions that have gone unstudied while SSRIs were prescribed to tens of millions. The psychiatric pharmaceutical complex has long resisted scrutiny of SSRI systemic effects beyond the brain. This study cracks that door open.

articles.title: Progesterone as a Depression Treatment: The Hormone Therapy the Antidepressant Industry Refuses to Study
articles.summary: Research linking chronic stress-driven neurological disruption to progesterone deficiency points toward a low-cost hormonal intervention for depression — one with no patent value and zero pharma funding behind it. While SSRIs generate over $15 billion annually, researchers studying progesterone's neuroprotective effects operate at the margins of a system designed to sell serotonin reuptake inhibitors, not fix root causes. The suppression isn't a conspiracy — it's a funding structure.

articles.title: Mitochondrial Dysfunction at the Root of Cancer and Chronic Inflammation — The Metabolic Theory Big Oncology Won't Fund
articles.summary: Mounting evidence connects mitochondrial failure directly to chronic inflammation and cancer risk, echoing the metabolic theory of cancer that has been sidelined since Otto Warburg first proposed it in the 1930s. The trillion-dollar oncology industry is built on genetic theories that justify targeted drug therapies — not metabolic interventions like dietary change, CO2 therapy, or mitochondrial support. Researchers advancing this work do so without NIH priority funding.

articles.title: Independence Blue Cross Pays $22.5M to Settle Medicare Advantage Fraud — Diagnosis Upcoding Scandal Exposes Systemic Billing Corruption
articles.summary: Independence Blue Cross will pay $22.5 million after allegedly retaining improper overpayments tied to unsupported diagnosis codes in its Medicare Advantage program — a practice that inflated government reimbursements while gaming patient risk scores. This is not an isolated case: Medicare Advantage upcoding fraud has cost taxpayers billions and is considered endemic to the industry. The question regulators won't answer is how many other insurers are doing the same thing and have not been caught.
